n: Taken from a letter Joseph Smith wrote to W. W. Phelps in Missouri. The Lord’s appointed clerk (John Whitmer at the time) must keep a history and record of Zion, including who consecrated property and received inheritances from the bishop.
The record should also note how people live, their faith and works, and anyone who falls away after receiving an inheritance.

f.g: Abandon the faith one once accepted.

n: Those who did not receive their land through consecration, as the Lord’s law required, should not be listed among God’s people in Zion. This law was meant to prepare the Saints for the coming day of judgment.

f.w: that he may tithe his people
f.g: Here “tithe” refers broadly to the consecrated offerings of the law of the Lord.

f.w: the day of vengeance and burning

n: Their family records were not to be kept in the Church’s records either.
Neither they nor their parents nor children will appear in “the book of the law of God”—the record of those who live the covenant.

f.w: the book of the law of God

f.g: Lord of armies—God as commander of heaven’s forces.

n: Joseph describes how revelation came: a still, small voice that whispers yet penetrates everything, sometimes making his very bones tremble.

The Lord will send “one mighty and strong” to set his house in order and assign inheritances. Church leaders in 1905 explained this prophecy was tied to the specific situation in Zion at the time and has often been misused by people claiming to be this figure.

f.g: A rod held by a ruler as a symbol of authority.
In old English, the inner self—the seat of feelings.

n: A warning drawn from Uzzah, who reached out to steady the ark and was struck down. Many understand it as a caution to Bishop Edward Partridge, who was then at odds with Joseph Smith; he later repented, and the warning did not fall on him.

f.g: To presume to correct the Lord’s work or his chosen leaders beyond one’s calling.

n: Those not written in the book of remembrance will have no inheritance in that day; they will be cut off and placed among unbelievers, where there is deep sorrow.
Joseph insists these words are not his own; what the Lord says, he will fulfill.
Priesthood holders and members who are not recorded, who have apostatized, or who have been cut off will not receive an inheritance among the Saints in that day.
They will be treated like the priests’ families in Ezra’s day who couldn’t find their genealogy and were excluded from the priesthood. Faithful record-keeping mattered then and now.

f.w: the second chapter and sixty-first and second verses of Ezra
